competing_explanation: The observed potency loss is more plausibly driven by batch age or manufacturing variability rather than storage temperature, since A3 shows RX-441 remains within spec (99.1% potency) at 25C/60% RH over 6 months.
hypothesis_statement: VERDICT: FALSE, because the controlled temperature-effect study (A4) held batch age constant and found no statistically significant effect of storage temperature on potency loss (p=0.71), directly refuting the causal claim.
predicted_outcome: If higher storage temperature were the cause of potency loss, holding batch age constant should show a statistically significant increase in potency loss at 40C versus 5C/25C.
refutation_criterion: A properly powered controlled study with batch age held constant showing a statistically significant temperature-driven potency loss gradient would falsify this verdict.
